rules.historical_meaning_only: Printed original CXL begins top of frame 643 and is distinct from travel occurrence/direction in CXXXIX.

rules.source_anchor_not_diplomatic: Planets who are Significators of Journeys
rules.historical_meaning_only: Lilly begins the alleged motive determination from planets already selected as significators of journeys.

rules.source_anchor_not_diplomatic: Houses in which Planets are posited
rules.historical_meaning_only: The house of each planetary travel significator is a second separate source of asserted journey causes.
The nature of the planet is used to classify possible motives and persons involved.
One possible travel-motive condition is another selected travel significator conjunct Saturn.
Saturn essential dignity is a different alternate condition for a Saturnian motive.
A third alternative is Saturn itself selected as the journey significator.
Lilly attributes searching/discovering mineral resources as a Saturn-like travel motive.
Recovery of an estate left by someone deceased is another asserted Saturn-like motivation.
Travel involving things traditionally classified under Saturn is another flexible historical result.
The source additionally lists older people, grave men, magistrates, gentlemen or merchants as Saturnian travel contacts.

rules.source_anchor_not_diplomatic: Gentlemen or Merchants of his condition
rules.historical_meaning_only: Saturnian social categories depend on the native's historical class/condition, not a universal objective status.
The chapter moves to a separate Jupiter-like travel significator and cause category.
Historical Jupiter travel motive includes travel concerning religion, not evidence of the native's actual beliefs.
Honour and social distinction are an alternative supposed motive in the same Jupiter source.
A legal dispute or pursuit is another Jupiter-associated alleged travel motivation.
Advancement in clerical institutions is another historical Jupiter motivation distinct from faith.
The chapter lists clerical, noble and judicial people associated with Jupiter-motivated travel.

rules.source_anchor_not_diplomatic: so of rest Planets as specified second House
rules.historical_meaning_only: The author explicitly refers to prior second-house planet associations for other travel motives, rather than spelling them out here.

rules.source_anchor_not_diplomatic: Next consider Houses wherein Planets posited
rules.historical_meaning_only: Lilly says to use the journey-signifier house to interpret reasons for travel after planetary natures.
One source circumstance requires a travel significator occupying the Ascendant/first house.
An alleged first-house outcome is personal curiosity or desire to see foreign countries.
A travel significator in second house gives another circumstance to be judged.
Commercial exchange/trade is attributed to second-house travel significators.
Financial enrichment is an additional alleged outcome of trade-related travel, distinct from motive.

rules.source_anchor_not_diplomatic: cause of Travell from nature of Significators and Houses
rules.historical_meaning_only: Lilly concludes that planetary natures and house placements jointly generate the historical travel motive judgment.

rules.source_anchor_not_diplomatic: HALY delivers these generall Aphorismes of Lord ninth
rules.historical_meaning_only: Lilly attributes a separate set of ninth-ruler-in-house aphorisms to Haly; Haly original text is not yet collated.
Every following house placement refers to ninth-house ruler, not the house ninth itself.
The first Haly-attributed condition is ruler of ninth in the first house.
The claimed outcome is frequent travel, different from any travel or staying abroad.
The second Haly-attributed condition places ruler of ninth in the second house.
Lilly transmits a claim of substantial travel profit in the second-house case.
The third Haly-attributed condition places ruler of ninth in the third house.
One third-house claim concerns intimate relations with unfamiliar women, not travel frequency.
Another distinct third-house claimed outcome is changing one's place of residence or location often.
The ninth ruler placed in fourth house is a separate Haly-attributed circumstance.
Lilly reports a hidden illness of parents as one outcome, distinct from travel motivation.
The same fourth-house placement is asserted to foretell death on a journey, without verified cases.
The fourth-house branch alleges two separate medical/lifespan events, not an observed combined case.
The fifth house is a different location of ninth ruler.
Haly-attributed fifth house rule alleges having children in another country, requiring independent natal parentage and geography data.
Sixth-house placement of ninth ruler forms another Haly-attributed motive/outcome category.
Lilly transmits a historical economic claim of gain through enslaved persons or servants.

rules.source_anchor_not_diplomatic: his Cattle shall fall sick in Travells
rules.historical_meaning_only: The Haly passage also alleges animal illness during travel, separate from human wealth.
Ninth ruler in the seventh house forms a different historical source circumstance.
One source outcome is obtaining a good wife, a moral label not a travel-success measure.
The chapter includes a sex/gender hierarchy assertion about a spouse's obedience, not independently validated psychology.
Eighth-house placement of ninth ruler is an independent source category.
A motivation to acquire an estate is ascribed to ninth ruler in eighth.
Travel across the sea is claimed alongside the eighth-house desire for property.
The original printed sequence stops after the eighth-house aphorism; no ninth-to-twelfth house equivalents appear here.

rules.source_anchor_not_diplomatic: CHAP CXLI Of Successe in Travell
rules.historical_meaning_only: A distinct numbered chapter on success or danger starts mid frame644 after the last Haly aphorism.
Only following CXLI opening words are retained as source-boundary evidence, not part of CXL travel causes.
